title: auth_exceptions_test.dart locks in inconsistent PII redaction between sibling exception types
rule: EH-5 (stable codes, not pre-formatted messages) / privacy consistency
why: The same test file proves the codebase knows raw emails shouldn't land in an exception's toString() — DuplicateEmailException's docstring (local_auth_service.dart:11-13) says so explicitly and this file asserts it (line 18) — yet asserts the opposite for EmailCollisionException (line 71), whose message is built as '$email is already in use' (upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart:12). The 3 current catch sites in upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart only branch on the exception's type today, but EH-1's global FlutterError.onError/PlatformDispatcher.onError handler forwards uncaught exceptions to AppLogger, typically by serializing toString(); if EmailCollisionException ever escapes a catch clause (new call site, refactor) the plaintext email reaches the logger/Crashlytics pipeline with nothing to stop it, unlike its sibling.
recommendation: Give EmailCollisionException the same email/redactedEmail split as DuplicateEmailException (keep the field, drop the raw address from message/toString), and update this test's assertion accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: EmailCollisionException.toString() no longer contains the raw email; a redactedEmail (or equivalent) accessor exists for callers that need a log-safe form
auth_exceptions_test.dart's EmailCollisionException group asserts the same log-safety property as the DuplicateEmailException group
